title: SharePoint agents: who can use them, what they can read and how they are billed
summary: The access controls, billing rates, retirement dates and reporting commands are supported by Microsoft documentation. Minor corrections should acknowledge Microsoft's differing audit-role guidance and complete the billing connection path.

claims.claim: SharePoint agents are AI agents that help users find information and insights on SharePoint sites, pages and document libraries.
claims.quote: Agents in SharePoint, powered by AI, help users quickly find information and insights on SharePoint sites, pages, and document libraries.

claims.where: What it is; Why it matters; Risks and limits: Agents inherit oversharing
claims.claim: Agent responses depend on the asking user's access permissions to the agent's data sources.
claims.quote: For users who access and use an agent in SharePoint, the agent's responses depend on each user's permissions to the agent's data sources.

claims.where: summary; What it is: Who can use agents; Cost and licensing: Licence
claims.claim: Users with a Microsoft Copilot licence can use agents in SharePoint.
claims.quote: Currently, users with a Microsoft Copilot license can use the agents.

claims.where: What it is: What can they draw on; Governance controls: How they interact
claims.claim: Site and file permissions control the information a user can obtain through a SharePoint agent.
claims.quote: You can control a user's access to the information when they use an agent by controlling their access to the site.

claims.where: What it is: What can they draw on; Governance controls: Not in the table
claims.claim: Restricted access control restricts site access to the users in the policy's group and consequently restricts the site's content in Copilot.
claims.quote: As a result, all access to the site is restricted to only the group of users specified in the policy. Accordingly, the content from the site is visible in Microsoft Copilot only for this restricted group of users.

claims.where: What it is: What can they draw on
claims.claim: Microsoft Purview DLP can govern content used by SharePoint agents.
claims.quote: To prevent selected files from being used by agents, use sensitivity labels along with Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP).

claims.where: What it is: Where do agents appear
claims.claim: Site owner settings control the agent that appears through the site's Agent icon.
claims.quote: Site owners can choose one main agent for their site. This agent opens when users select the Agent icon in the global header.

claims.claim: The legacy SharePoint agent is a .agent file saved where it was created.
claims.quote: Every agent you create in SharePoint is a .agent file saved in the location where you create it.

claims.claim: Permissions on the .agent file determine who can access or edit the legacy agent.
claims.quote: The permissions on the .agent file determine who can access or edit the agent.

claims.where: What it is: Two formats; What to check
claims.claim: Existing .agent files continue to work until the end of March 2027.
claims.quote: Existing agents in the .agent file format will continue to work across SharePoint, Microsoft Teams, and the Copilot app until the end of March 2027.

claims.claim: Starting in mid-November 2026, agents for SharePoint and OneDrive are created in Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder.
claims.quote: Starting in mid-November 2026, you'll use Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder to create agents for SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.claim: The new agent creation experience no longer saves a .agent file.
claims.quote: However, creating an agent no longer saves a .agent file in SharePoint or OneDrive.

claims.claim: Microsoft is retiring the .agent file format, not agents in SharePoint.
claims.quote: No, only the .agent file format is being retired.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio agents published to SharePoint do not need recreating because of the format retirement.
claims.quote: You don't need to recreate Copilot Studio agents published to SharePoint because of this change.

claims.claim: Upgraded agents are governed through Microsoft Agent 365.
claims.quote: Users can monitor agents in this builder, and administrators can govern, analyze, and manage agents through Microsoft Agent 365.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls: How they interact; controls[3].governs
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery limits a site's content in tenant-wide discovery and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery affects organization-wide search experiences (SharePoint home, Office.com, Bing) and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, including experiences that rely on tenant-wide content discovery.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls: How they interact; controls[3].governs
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery removes AI entry points, including agent creation, from restricted SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: Users don't see entry points such as the Copilot button, AI actions menus (including creating agents), or Create pages with AI.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Restricted Content Discovery; controls[3].note
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery leaves permissions unchanged and permits users to continue accessing content directly.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't change existing permissions. Users who already have access to content can continue to access that content directly.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls: How they interact
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery does not stop Copilot summarising an already-open document.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't affect experiences that operate on content that's already in use by the user, such as summarizing an open document.

claims.claim: Agents in SharePoint do not require activation.
claims.quote: Agents in SharePoint don't require activation.

claims.claim: When pay-as-you-go billing is configured, administrators control agent access through the security groups assigned to the billing policy.
claims.quote: Or, if your organization has the pay-as-you-go billing set up, you can control who can access agents through the security groups assigned to the billing policy.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing: Pay-as-you-go
claims.claim: The unlicensed-user route is pay-as-you-go through an Azure resource used whenever a user without a Copilot licence uses a SharePoint agent.
claims.quote: To use pay-as-you-go billing, you need to first set up SharePoint agents as a resource in Azure. That resource is used whenever a user without a Microsoft Copilot license uses a SharePoint agent.

claims.claim: Interactive generative answers, tenant graph grounding and agent actions by authenticated Microsoft Copilot users in Microsoft 365 apps and services are included at no extra cost.
claims.quote: Interactive use of generative answers, tenant graph grounding and agent actions by authenticated Microsoft Copilot users, in Microsoft 365 apps and services, are included at no extra cost.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: rate table, Generative answer
claims.claim: The billing page lists generative answers at 2 messages for autonomous use.
claims.quote: | Generative answer | 2 messages | No charge | 2 messages |

claims.where: Cost and licensing: rate table, Tenant graph grounding
claims.claim: The billing page lists tenant graph grounding for messages at 10 messages for autonomous use.
claims.quote: | Tenant graph grounding for messages | 10 messages | No charge | 10 messages |

claims.claim: Each SharePoint agent interaction uses 12 messages to answer a single complex prompt.
claims.quote: SharePoint agents are grounded in the tenant graph, so each interaction with a SharePoint agent uses 12 messages (10 messages for tenant graph grounding, and 2 messages for generative answers) to respond to a single complex prompt from the user.

claims.claim: Tenant graph grounding is optional and can be turned on or off for each agent.
claims.quote: This capability is optional, and you can turn it on or off for each agent.

claims.claim: SharePoint agent usage charges appear under the Copilot Studio meter on the invoice.
claims.quote: Charges of SharePoint agent usage appear under the Copilot Studio meter in your invoice.

claims.claim: Microsoft Cost Management provides a feature-level usage-charge breakdown including SharePoint agents.
claims.quote: However, in Microsoft cost management, you can see a detailed breakdown by feature, including SharePoint agents.

claims.claim: A budget with alerts for SharePoint agent spending can be created in Microsoft Cost Management.
claims.quote: You can quickly create a budget under Monitoring > Budgets for your selected scope. ... Select Alert conditions to set up the budget alert conditions.

claims.claim: The SharePoint billing page lists SharePoint administrator as a prerequisite for setting up SharePoint agents as an Azure resource.
claims.quote: To set up SharePoint agents as a resource in Azure, you need to have at least the following permissions as: ... A SharePoint administrator

claims.claim: The general Copilot pay-as-you-go setup guide requires Billing Administrator, AI Administrator or Global Administrator for its tasks.
claims.quote: You must have one of the following roles to complete the tasks in this article: ... Billing Administrator ... AI Administrator ... Global Administrator

claims.claim: Both setup guides require Azure Owner or Contributor rights to the subscription.
claims.quote: You must have Owner or Contributor rights to the Azure subscription and resource group.

claims.claim: Both setup guides require Azure Owner or Contributor rights to the resource group.
claims.quote: Owner or Contributor Azure roles to an Azure resource group linked to the same Azure subscription

claims.claim: The SharePoint billing page says the Azure Owner or Contributor roles are needed only during billing setup.
claims.quote: You only need the Owner or Contributor Azure roles during the billing setup process.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Reporting licences; controls[4].note

claims.quote: To generate and view these reports, ensure the organization has the SharePoint Advanced Management add-on SKU or Microsoft Copilot license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Reporting licences; controls[2].note

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery can be applied only to SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: You can only apply this feature to SharePoint sites.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Restricted Content Discovery

claims.quote: It's not supported for OneDrive sites.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Restricted Content Discovery

claims.quote: For sites with more than 500,000 items, an update to Restricted Content Discovery could take more than a week to fully process and reflect in search and Copilot experiences.

claims.where: Risks and limits: DLP cannot yet use a label on the agent file

claims.quote: You can't yet add a sensitivity label directly to the .agent file.

claims.where: Risks and limits: DLP cannot yet use a label on the agent file

claims.quote: Each billing policy can currently have one security group. Support for multiple security groups will be available soon.

claims.claim: The SharePoint billing page states a limit of 10 billing policies.

claims.quote: You can create up to 50 billing policies for your tenant.

claims.claim: The general Copilot pay-as-you-go setup page explicitly applies to SharePoint agents.
claims.quote: This article applies to: ... Microsoft Copilot Chat ... SharePoint agents

claims.claim: For the security-group billing-policy configuration on the SharePoint access page, only users in the assigned security group have access through that policy.
claims.quote: Only users in the security group assigned to the billing policy have access to agents.

claims.claim: The Copilot-node setup page also documents an All users choice on Choose users.
claims.quote: On the Choose users page, select All users or a Specific group. If you select Specific group, search for and add a single group.
